subject: Physics
central_question: How do work, kinetic and potential energy, power and conservation laws provide a scalar description of motion and interactions, including collisions?
in_scope_units: 5.1 Introduction and 5.1.1 Scalar Product — physical meanings and the dot product needed to define work.
5.2 Notions of Work and Kinetic Energy: The Work–Energy Theorem.
5.5 Work Done by a Variable Force and 5.6 Work–Energy Theorem for a Variable Force.
5.7 Concept of Potential Energy and conservative forces.
5.11 Collisions, including elastic/inelastic collisions and one- and two-dimensional cases.
banned_topics: Vector product/cross product as a rotational-motion topic

known_pitfalls.claim: Any applied force necessarily does work.
known_pitfalls.correction: Work requires displacement and depends on the component of force along displacement; it is zero for zero displacement or perpendicular force.

known_pitfalls.claim: Action and reaction forces always do equal and opposite work.
known_pitfalls.correction: The forces are equal and opposite, but the displacements of the two bodies can differ, so the works need not be equal and opposite.

known_pitfalls.claim: Kinetic energy is conserved in every collision.
known_pitfalls.correction: Linear momentum is conserved for an isolated collision; kinetic energy is conserved only in an elastic collision.

known_pitfalls.claim: kWh is a unit of power.
known_pitfalls.correction: kWh is a unit of energy; power is measured in watt, with 1 W = 1 J s⁻¹.
